nodes.label: Ceramic Infrared Heat Emitter Lamp
nodes.description: Studio photograph on black of a white ceramic infrared heat emitter with an E27 screw base. The emitting face is a flat disc with a moulded concentric spiral/labyrinth relief that follows the embedded resistive heating element and maximises radiating surface area. Emits infrared heat with no visible light.
nodes.rationale: A ceramic IR emitter is preferred over an incandescent brooder bulb because it delivers radiant heat without emitting visible light, so the thermal environment can be regulated without disturbing the day/night light cycle of the occupants — and, for a vision-based system, without corrupting the camera's illumination conditions.

nodes.label: Thermal Actuation (Radiant Heating Control)
nodes.description: The control action of raising enclosure temperature by radiant infrared output, switched on demand to hold a temperature setpoint.
nodes.rationale: Radiant rather than convective heating is used so heat reaches occupants directly and is not immediately carried away by the ventilation airflow, letting heating and ventilation be regulated semi-independently.
